Mom's Health Information and Helpers, in One Place

A one-page inventory of the diagnoses, medications, doctors and helpers you already know about, and the blanks.

Download PDF

The medication list is on the fridge, the doctor's number is in Mom's address book, and your sister is the one who knows who drives her on Thursdays.

This page doesn't ask you to understand any of it. It asks where each thing is, how recent it is, and who has it. Fill it in with Mom if you can. Most of it is hers.

What to collectWhere it isIts dateWho has it
Her diagnoses and ongoing conditions, as a list
Medication list: prescriptions, over-the-counter items, vitamins and supplements
Treatments or therapies she has now, and their schedule
Her doctors and specialists, with phone numbers
Her pharmacy
Upcoming appointments
Family, friends and neighbors who help, and what each one does
Any paid help she uses now, and how to reach them
Notes on any falls during the past year
Notes on changes the family has noticed during the past year
What she has told you about her care preferences, in writing
Names of local care providers you've collected so far

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Anything above with an empty line. Put a name next to each.

For example No list of her medications in one place. Karen will ask Mom whether they can write one out together on Sunday.

How to use it

  • Write the date on each item: when the list was written or last updated. If it has no date, write “undated.”
  • Don't rewrite or summarize a record here. Just say where it is.
  • Ask Mom before you copy or share anything of hers.
  • Bring this page to her next appointment, if she'd like you there.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any record, diagnosis or instruction means. If you read something you don't understand, that's a question for the person who wrote it. Nothing here is medical, legal, financial or tax advice.
